content: A centimetre, also spelled as centimeter in American English and symbolized as cm, is a unit of length within the metric system. It is defined as one-hundredth of a metre, which is the current SI base unit for length. The prefix centi in the International System of Units (SI) denotes a factor of 10^-2. Therefore, a centimetre can be expressed as 10 × 10^-3 metres in engineering notation or 1E-2 metres in scientific notation. This equivalence also translates to 10 × 1 millimetre or 1 metre divided by 100. The centimetre was historically the base unit of length in the now-obsolete centimetre-gram-second (CGS) system of units. While SI prefixes for factors of 10^3, such as milli and kilo, are often preferred by technical professionals for many physical quantities, the centimetre remains a practical and widely used unit of length for everyday measurements. For reference, the width of an adult human fingernail is approximately one centimetre. In terms of volume, one cubic centimetre (cm³) is equivalent to one millilitre (mL) under the current SI system. Additionally, in Canadian cartography, centimetres are commonly used to convert map scales into real-world distances, such as kilometres. Unicode provides specific symbols for the centimetre and its derived units to ensure compatibility with Chinese, Japanese, and Korean (CJK) character sets. These include: Centimetre (cm): Unicode code 339D Square centimetre (㎠): Unicode code 33A0 Cubic centimetre (㎤): Unicode code 33A4 These symbols are particularly useful when used with East Asian fixed-width CJK fonts, as they are designed to match the size of a single Chinese character.
